Md. Kalim Zillah Mazunider, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Moulavi Md Wahidullah, Md Shahed Razmul Bari with Md Shahidul Islam, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Fazal Hossain (Md) and others ----- Petitioners
VS.
Md Helal Mia & others ----- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
10. The opposite party pre-emptor has filed a counter affidavit against the aforesaid supplementary affidavit filed by the rule petitioner on 10-2-2009 and wherein he has annexed a registered deed of agreement being No. 9770 dated 21-9-1959 annexing the same as Annexure X and he has also annexed a sa f kabala deed of reconveyance executed by aforesaid Shamsuddin in favour of Abdul Aziz. on 21-9-1959 being saf kabala deed No. 17697 dated 26-12-1963 and annexed the same marking the same as Annexure Y. And the opposite party has also annexed copies of a series of survey Khatian No. 91 RS No.3087 and RS No. 3280 present Dhaka city settlement Plot Nos. 2311, 2839, 2840 and 2838 within Mouza Kadamtali under Police Station Shyampur now Kadamtali, Dhaka Photostat copy of Khatian being No. 91 having been annexed and marked as Annexure Z, Z1, Z3 and Z4. Thereafter today while I was going to deliver the judgment, Mr Mazumder has again come up with an affidavit in reply on behalf of the petitioner to the counter affidavit filed by the opposite party No. 1 on 11-2-2009. Mr Mazumder on 16-2-2009 filed an affidavit in reply to the counter affidavit filed by the opposite party No. 1 on 11-2-2009 wherein he has annexed the application of 3-6-1999 filed before the appellate Court by the appellant marking the same as Annexure B and he has also filed certified copy of the written objection filed by the respondent opposing the said petition dated 3-6-1999 marking the same as Annexure B1 wherein according to Mr Mazumder the respondent stated in the said written objection that is father of the respondent Abdul Aziz got the said Plot No. 951/1425 together with some other land measuring in all 1.26 acre of land by way of reconveyance from Shamsuddin to whom earlier the father of the respondent sold out the said property by a Saf Kabala deed dated 21-9-1959 followed by a registered agreement, registered on the same date between the same parties for reconveyance of the said land on receiving the consideration money and this money was returned. But the father of pre-emptor respondent because of the simplicity did not get the Saf Kabala (reconveyance deed) registered which has been annexed has Annexure B1 and Mr. Mazumder has also annexed Photostat copy of plaint and written objection etc. of Title Suit No.245 of 2007 marking the same as Annexure C. wherein one Mst. Happy Begum filed this suit as plaintiff against the present pre-emptor opposite party No. 1 Helal Uddin and 29 others imp leading them as defendant marking the same as Annexure C. Today while I have taken the case for delivering the judgment Mr. Majumder has filed another supplementary affidavit today serving copy on the other side at 11.10 am on 22-2-2009 wherein he has annexed a copy of the petition filed by the appellant before the appellate Court on 3-6-1999 marking the same as Annexure B 7 and certified copy of written objection filed by pre-emptor respondent on 28-3-2000 marking the same as B and B1 and he has also filed the certified copy of the order sheet of the learned appellate Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 63 of 1993 starting from order at serial No. 41 dated 3-6-1999 to 29-5-2002 the date on which the learned appellate Judge deliver the judgment marking the same as Annexure C to show that the learned appellate Judge did not pass any order on the said application of the appellant dated 3-6-1999 and Mr. Majumder in this respect submits that after filing of this application the Court ought to have passed an order either accepting or rejecting the said application but without passing any order on the said application the learned appellate Judge delivered his judgment without deciding the said application whereas if this application would have been properly considered would have helped the learned appellate Judge to set aside the judgment and order passed by the learned trial Judge because in this application the appellant has mentioned about the disposal of the property appertaining to Plot No. 951/1425 by the pre-emptor and by this sale he has lost right, title and character of a adjoining owner thus if the petition would have been considered it would have changed the fate of the case. 

 14. Mr Wahidullah has also drawn my attention to Annexure Z series which are the attested RS Khatian No. 2488 dated 6-8-1999 of revisional survey operation which contain the name of present pre-emptor petitioner together with other legal heirs of said Abdul Aziz. He has also submitted as he mentioned in paragraph 4 of the counter affidavit stating that the pre-emptor possessed the contiguous land being Khatian No. 91, RS No. 3087 and RS No. 3280 present Dhaka city settlement Plot Nos. 2311, 2839, 2840 and 2838 within Mouza Kadamtali under Police Station Shyampur now Kadamtali Dhaka and in support of his statement he has annexed all copies of the said Khatian. He submits that this Khatian has got presumptive value and which lends support to the possession of the pre-emptor in the adjacent plot of the preempted land. Mr. Wahidullah submits that this documents filed by way of Annexure with the counter affidavit in replay to the rule petition and supplementary affidavit filed by the rule petitioner may kindly be taken into consideration as the pre-emptor as respondent in the appeal filed written objection in response to the petition filed by the appellant in respect of this fact of sale by the father of the pre-emptor petitioner respondent and this pre-emptor opposite parties as respondent in the said written objection clearly mentioned that his father mortgaged the said property with Shamsuddin by registered deed No. 9770 dated 21-9-1959 property being in total 1.26 acres of land appertaining to plot No. 951/1425 being 83 decimals and plot No. 1086 land measuring 43 decimals which appertains to Khatian No. 143 and it is specifically mention that the said deed was a deed of mortgage though it was registered as Saf Kabala it was deed of mortgage for an amount of Taka 700 followed by registered agreement, registered on the same date that is 21-9-1959 and it is also stated in the same written objection that the father of the pre-emptor opposite party subsequently return the said Taka 700 to the mortgagee (purchaser Shamsuddin) within the stipulated time and got back the said property in his ownership and possession. But inadvertently it was mention in the petition that the father of the pre-emptor petitioner because of his simplicity did not get the reconvened Saf Kabala registered but Mr. Wahidullah submits that through inadvertence though the pre-emptor respondent could not produce the said deed of reconvene as well as deed of agreement which he has been able to collect subsequently in the year 2007 after vigorous searching and he got certified copy on 19-3-2007 which has been annexed as annexed to the counter affidavit. Mr. Wahidullah submits that since this point at least having been stated before the appellate Court by filing written objection and now it is submitted before this Court by way of counter affidavit by swearing affidavit and annexing those with the counter affidavit this Court for ends of justice can taken into consideration these documents which is most vital point for determination of the status of the pre-emptor as owner of the contiguous plot of land of the case land. He prays that in view of the facts and circumstances of the present case the rule be discharged. 

 15. I have given my anxious consideration to the submission made at the Bar. I have gone through the rule petition, the impugned judgment and judgment of the trial Court as well. After going through the impugned judgment, I find that the learned appellate Judge has framed as many as five independent issues by himself while disposing of the appeal and after proper and meticulous discussion of the issues and on proper evaluation and discussion of each and every point of issues that has been disposed of by the learned trial Judge. The learned appellate Judge came to his finding and decision and affirmed the judgment of the learned trial Judge and after going through the impugned judgment I do not find material substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment as per provision of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil procedure and it suffers from misreading and non-reading of evidences on record. Regarding the fact of misreading and non-reading of evidences on record as it is submitted by the learned Advocate of the petitioner, I am unable to discuss and reassess those because of the fact that the learned Advocate for the petitioner a t the time of issuance of the rule did not obtain order calling for the lower Courts record. So since the lower Courts record is not before me I am not in a position to go through the evidences on record as the lower Courts record is not before me. But after going through the judgment of the trial Court I find that the learned trial Judge has very meticulously and vividly discussed each and every point and fact in issue and came to his finding and decision deciding all the 5 issues in favour of the pre-emptor petitioner including the issues of maintainability and the point of conjoined of parties and means defect of parties. The learned trial Judge has very clearly and distinctly after discussing the evidences on record reached a t his decision to decide those issues in favour of the plaintiff. Inasmuch as the learned trial Judge has also very candidly and clearly discuss about the legal position of the pre-emptor to have the right to file the pre-emption case and very clearly found that the pre-emptor is in possession of the adjacent southern plot of the case plot (pre-empted plot) by giving his reasoning and with reference to evidences on record specially he gave reference to CS Map that has been produced by the opposite party before the Court and which clearly shows that Plot No. 951/1425 is adjacent southern plot of the case Plot No. 951/1425. And it is also avail-able from the CS Khatian i.e. Exhibit 1 that Hasan Ali the predecessor of Md Ahsan Ali who is the vendor of the pre-emptor opposite party has been shown in the northern boundary of the said Plot No. 951/1425 of the pre-mentor’s grandfather late Usman. So I find that the learned trial Judge has very meticulously and very carefully discussed each and every piece of evidence while he was deciding the issue in favour of the plaintiff and the learned appellate Judge being the last Court of fact has framed independent issue and discussed all this very important issues like maintainability of the suit and defect of parties and question of limitation and also the point of part pre-emption as prayed for. And after meticulous discussion and proper evaluation of the evidences on record and with reference to the judgment of the learned trial Judge and findings given by the learned trial Judge while allow the pre-emption the learned appellate Judge was pleased to affirmed the judgment of the learned trial Judge by disallowing the appeal. In my opinion while the learned appellate judge is affirming the judgment of the trial Court he need not discussion each and every point and he can even deliver a judgment by discussing each and every point that has been discussed and found by the learned trial Judge. 

 16. In respect of submission of Mr Mazumder to the effect that the pre-emptor had no locus standi to filed the pre-emption case this point has also been very categorically and candidly dismissed by the learned trial Judge after discussing the evidences on record and the learned appellate Judge also has discussed the same point and affirm the same as the first issue as to whether the suit is maintainable or not. So, I find that this point that has been raised by Mr Mazumder also not being substantiated by sufficient papers and document on record. The next point of submission that has been made by Mr Mazumder that the pre-emptes appellate filed an application on 3-6-1999 stating therein some facts specially the fact that the father of the pre-emptor namely Abdul Aziz sold out the said plot of land i.e. 951/1425 to one Shamsuddin and since he has sold out the property the pre-emptor had no locus standi to file the pre-emption case. And this petition was filed before the learned appellate Judge on 3-6-1999 the learned appellate Judge on receipt of this application kept few days as many as 4 days for hearing of the same but he did not dispose of the same rather with-out disposing the same he has heard the appeal and delivered the judgment without disposing the said petition in the negative or positive. Mr Mazumder has filed a certified copy the said petition and the written objection against that filed by the pre-emptor opposite party in the appellate Court as respondent. I have gone through the said petition which has been marked as annexure as well as the written objection, filed by the pre-emptor respondent dated 28-3-2000 and he order sheet of the Court which has been marked as Annexures B, B1 and C with the supplementary affidavit dated 22-2-2009. After going through the aforesaid petition of the pre-emptee appellant dated 3-6-1999, I find that the said application did not contain as annexure. any copy of the alleged said to be deed No. 9770 dated 21-9-1959 by which the father of the pre-emptor sold out his property appertaining to Plot No. 951/1425 only this number has been mentioned but no copy of the said deed was submitted before the Court nor any petition for allowing the appellant to adduce additional evidence in this respect was filed before the Court. By merely filing a petition and only stating the Saf Kabala number of the father of the pre-emptor disposed of the property without brining any formal prove or evidence before the Court as per provision of law the appellant made a prayer that this fact be made a ground in the Memo of appeal. So after going through this petition as well as order sheet, I find that the learned Appellant judge was right in not considering this application as it was not filed nor any prayer was made as per relevant provision of the Code of Civil Procedure. So the learned appellate Judge did not consider this application as it did not call for any interference by the learned appellate Judge in the appellate forum beyond the legal procedure. But Mr Mazumder the learned Advocate by filing a supplementary affidavit dated 10-2-2009 has filed a certified copy of the said deed of conveyance i.e. the deed No. 9770 by which the father of the pre-emptor sold out his said property to one Shamsuddin Ahmed, make the same Annexure A with the supplementary affidavit and he has very candidly submitted that in view of this Saf Kabala deed the pre-emptor opposite party had no right, title or interest of file Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and he Courts below committed error of law by allowing the pre-emption case. But I find that this document had neither been placed before the trial Court nor before the appellate Court but only mere statement was made before the appellate Court by tiling an application which the learned appellate Judge did not consider and it was not filed in accordance with law and I further find that by filing a counter affidavit dated 11-2-2009 the pre-emptor opposite party his filed a certified copy of an agreement being deed No. 9771 wherein it has been decided and agreed upon by the parties to the sale deed No. 9770 i.e. the sale deed about which Mr Mazumder has been stressing that in view of this deed all right, title and interest of pre-emptor has been exhausted and have no right to file pre-emption miscellaneous case. But from this annexure X, I find that on the same day an agreement was executed by said Shamsuddin Ahmed under taking to recovery the said purchased land of Kabala No. 9770 to the said vendor within four years of the date of Kabala and the agreement was registered of the same date and within four years time which evident from exhibit Y being a Saf Kabala deed being No. 17697 dated 26-12-1963 it appears that the same self property has been reconveyed to the father of the pre-emptor by said Shamsuddin on receiving back the said consideration money of Taka 700 and in this respect I would like to mention further that the learned trial Judge found possession of the pre-emptor in pursuance of CS record (Khatian) as well as draft publication Khatian of the SA record which stands in the name of the pre-emptor and now I find from the Annexure Z series which has been marked as annexed which the counter affidavit by the pre-emptor opposite party and this Z series shows that the RS Khatian as well as the Dhaka city survey Khatian has been published in the name of the pre-emptor and his other co-sharer which a t least bears presumptive value in respect of possession of the pre-emptor opposite party which he has claimed as per his petition of pre-emption that means all along possession of the suit land as well as his own plot of land being plot No. 951/1425 and the learned trial Judge after vivid discussion of all the evidences on record arrived at his finding that the pre-emptor is owner in possession of the adjacent plot No. 951/1425 and it is more clarified in view of the Annexure filed by Mr Wahidullah by filing the counter affidavit and annexure those document for this reason. In rebutting this counter affidavit Mr Mazumder has filed an affidavit in reply annexing the aforesaid petition dated 3-6-1999 filed by the appellant before the appellate Court and the written objection that has been filed by the pre-emptor respondent wherein as it is submitted by Mr Mazumder and after going the same I find there was line at page 6 of the certified copy of the said written objection that “কিন্তু মজহরের পিতা সরলতা কারণে ইহা রেজিষ্ট্রি করিয়া নেন নাই। But he has also annexed Photostat copy of certified copy of a Title Suit being No. 245 of 2007 pending in the Court of Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka being Annexure C wherein one Mst Happy Begum being the plaintiff has filed the suit against the pre-emptor Helal Uddin and others claiming ownership of the said land against them. But I do not find any justification or reason to take into consideration this case filed a 3rd party against the pre-emptor where-in the plaintiff claims to have purchase this property from the legal heirs of said Shamsuddin whereas from Annexure Y as filed by the pre-emptor opposite party with his counter affidavit the right, title and possession of the said Shamsuddin had been exhausted with the execution and registration of the said deed of reconveyance in favour of his seller Abdul Aziz. So, this case of Mst. Happy Begum is coming in no way to any help to the pre-emptee petitioner although Mr Mazumder very strenuously tried to argued on all this point but I do not find any cogent reason to accept all this things and I do not find much material force in the argument of Mr Mazumder on this point and in revisional jurisdiction I have taken into consideration the counter affidavit as well as the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner as well as the counter affidavit filed by the opposite party. Only because since the petitioner at the final stage of the case have come with some new facts and filed certain document praying for consideration of the same by this Court. So, I have to take into consideration the counter affidavit as well as the document that been filed by way of Annexure with the counter affidavit by the opposite party and the citation that has been referred to by Mr Mazumder the learned Advocate for the petitioner being case reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162 wherein our lordships decided and found that "If there is misreading of evidence and non-consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional Court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case." This finding of our lordship's in the appellate Division is not coming to very much assistance to the argument advanced by Mr Mazumder because after going through the judgment of both the Courts below, I do not find any omission or material irregularities to have been committed by the Courts below calling for interference by this Court. Moreover, the point of misreading and non-reading of evidences on record being agitated by Mr Mazumder but unfortunately at the time of issuance of the rule the petitioner did not obtain order calling for the lower Court record and since the lower Court record is not before me, I cannot go through the evidences on record and I have to bend upon the veracity of the judgment of both the Court below and after going through both the judgment of the Courts below, I find that both the judgment are well discussed and well founded judgment wherein interference of the revisional Court is not call for in any way or manner as such I am unable to accept the contention of Mr Mazumder. Rather I find substances in the submission of Mr Wahidullah and the citation referred to by him being 12 BLD (AD) 48 = 44 DLR (AD) 98 which is in agreement with his submission and the case of the opposite party No. 1.
